Question 1
?

The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by s(t)=2t3−3t2+2t, where t is measured in seconds. Find the particle's acceleration at t=2 seconds.

a
21m/s2
b
12m/s2
c
18m/s2
d
24m/s2
e
14m/s2
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of displacement: s'(t)=6t^2-6t+2 and s''(t)=12t-6. At t=2, the acceleration is 24-6=18 m/s².

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t$, where $t$ is measured in seconds.  Find the particle's acceleration at $t=2$ seconds.
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+2t) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-6t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-6t+2) \\  & =12t-6\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the acceleration at time $t=2$, we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =12(2)-6 \\  & =24-6 \\  & =18\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration when $t=2$ seconds is $18\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-6{t}^{2}+2{t}^{3}) \\  & =-12t+6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12t+6{t}^{2}) \\  & =-12+12t \\  & =12(t-1)\end{aligned}
$$

a(t)=t−1t
c
a(t)=t+1t
